newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent firmer on tight gas oil, technicals.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent firmer on tight gas oil, technicals.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were firmer on Monday as bullish short-term technical factors boosted a market already supported by tight gas oil markets and uncertainty over the possibility of renewed Iraqi exports, traders said.
August Brent stood at $18.38 a barrel up at 1140 GMT, 29 cents firmer and just below resistance at $18.39/$18.40. August gas oil was a healthy $3.25 up at $165.25 a tonne.
"Fundamentally nothing's changed this morning - there was no news on the weekend from Iraq - it is just the trend and momentum carrying us higher," one dealer said.
Dealers said a tight gas oil market in the Rotterdam area had enabled refined product to overcome nearby resistance and put in a strong performance.

This had dragged Brent higher with it, they said, adding that crude was now bumping its head against resistance at $18.39/$18.40, an imperfect double top formed on the August Brent chart on July 8 and 9.

U.N. officials declined to comment on Monday on the outcome of their meeting with Iraqi officials in Baghdad on Sunday to discuss details of Iraq's aid distribution plan which both Iraqi and U.N. officials say is necessary before Iraqi crude exports under an oil-for-food scheme resume.
The absence of fresh news from Iraq on Monday was providing a bullish backdrop to the energy complex, chart analysts said.

Peter Sceats at CharTech-MCS said in a weekly technical report on Brent: "If any mini up move does form, within the context of a market which is still south of $18.40/$18.50, it is likely that the move will be a sell opportunity given the weight of the background technicals."
